reasoning: Four acts in one turn, read to the end before acting on any of them. (1) Correction: the modification is in flight and unclosed, and the message raises its acceptance bar - it must now be shown not to swell the shipped bundle (or to load the extra weight per platform) and not to break anything a user sees. That is a constraint added to work already running, so it is replanned in place on its own checkpoint and adds no row; the acceptable alternative he names, dynamic loading by platform type, is part of that same constraint, not a separate idea, so nothing is shelved. (2) Observation: 'the prover should have caught this too' is a judgment about the product - a stated gap in what the prover checks - and it stays worth knowing long after this modification lands, so it does not dissolve into the neighbouring clause as mere grounds. (3) Instruction: 'by the way check' asks now for that gap to be investigated. It is a result someone could want on its own - the prover's coverage could ship or be cancelled without touching this modification - so it is the one new piece of work this turn produces, with its own goal and sheet. (4) Question: 'I don't know if that's real or not' asks whether a prover can catch bundle growth at all; it is answered in words, not converted into a second row. Dimensions are named only where something must change: quality and regressions (the check that would have caught the growth does not exist), and architecture/operations (bundle weight and the platform-conditional loading he offers as the remedy). Product prover for the class-based hunt over its own coverage, test author for the check that fails on growth and passes without it, independent verifier because the size and no-breakage claim cannot rest on the self-report of whoever made the modification. Architect joins only if the answer turns out to be splitting the load by platform. The feasibility doubt gets a straight answer in the same reply: a byte budget on the built artifact is measurable and cheap, so that half is real; 'nothing breaks for the user' is only as real as the regressions already covered, and that limit is stated rather than promised away.
